questions.question: Name the five processes of nutrition in order and define each in one sentence.
questions.expected_answer: Ingestion: taking food into the mouth. Digestion: breaking large, insoluble food molecules into small, soluble molecules, mechanically and chemically with enzymes. Absorption: the movement of small, soluble molecules through the wall of the small intestine into the blood (and lymph). Assimilation: the use of absorbed molecules by body cells for energy, growth and repair. Egestion: the removal of undigested food as faeces through the anus.

questions.question: Name the four accessory organs of digestion and state the product or role of each.
questions.expected_answer: Salivary glands: produce saliva, which moistens food and starts starch digestion. Liver: produces bile, which breaks fat into small droplets. Gall bladder: stores bile and releases it into the duodenum. Pancreas: produces pancreatic juice with enzymes for starch, proteins and fats, released into the duodenum.

questions.question: Explain why diarrhoea is dangerous for young children and describe how it is treated and prevented.
questions.expected_answer: Diarrhoea causes rapid loss of water and salts, leading to dehydration, which can kill a small child within a day. Treatment: give oral rehydration solution (1 litre clean water, 8 level teaspoons sugar, half a level teaspoon salt) frequently, continue feeding and breastfeeding, and go to a clinic if the child is drowsy, cannot drink or has blood in the stool. Prevention: clean water, proper sanitation, handwashing with soap, safe food handling and the rotavirus vaccine.
